title: California's 8th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for California's 8th Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat John Garamendi against Republican challenger Rudy Recile. The district covers parts of Contra Costa and Solano Counties in the northern Bay Area, including Richmond, Vallejo, Fairfield, and Antioch. Garamendi, who has held the seat since 2009 and served in elected office since 1974, advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 54.4% of the vote, while Recile, a retired U.S. Army Major and small business owner, secured 27.8%. Cook Political Report rates the general election race as Solid Democratic, reflecting the district's strong Democratic lean (D+19 Cook PVI).
polling_note: No independent general election polls were publicly available for this race at the time of research. Cook Political Report rates the district as Solid Democratic, and no recent matchup polling between Garamendi and Recile was found.

candidates.name: John Garamendi
candidates.summary: John Garamendi is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 8th Congressional District, first elected in a 2009 special election. He previously served as California Lieutenant Governor (2007-2009), Insurance Commissioner (1991-1994, 2003-2006), State Senator (1976-1990), and State Assemblymember (1974-1976). A graduate of UC Berkeley and Harvard Business School, he served in the Peace Corps in Ethiopia and is the top Democrat on the House Armed Services Subcommittee on Readiness.

candidates.name: Rudy Recile
candidates.summary: Rudy Recile is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in California's 8th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army Major with 26 years of military service, he is a first-generation American and small business owner who founded YCDI Corp, a website development company. Recile holds a BA from Eastern Illinois University and an MS in Quality Systems Management, and previously worked as a Data Manager and Instructor for the U.S. Department of Agriculture. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 27.8% of the vote to challenge incumbent John Garamendi in the general election.
